title: Hybrid Address Intelligence: From ~5% to 80%+ Accuracy
blurb: An Eircode-anchored hybrid pipeline that cleans noisy input, applies deterministic parsing, and uses controlled LLM handling for ambiguity with confidence scoring and review, processing about 1,000 addresses a day at over 80% accuracy, up from roughly 5-6%.
result: Accuracy improved from about 5% to over 80%
whoFor: Last-mile delivery and logistics operations where address data arrives messy, inconsistent, and hard to route on reliably.
challengeIntro: Delivery routing is only as good as the address data behind it, and in practice that data arrives noisy: inconsistent formatting, missing detail, and ambiguity that left only a small fraction of addresses reliably usable without manual correction.
challengePoints: Roughly 5 to 6 percent of incoming addresses were reliably accurate as received.
Manual correction did not scale with delivery volume.
Ambiguous addresses needed judgment, not just stricter parsing rules.
Eircode, the addressing standard for the market, was underused as a source of truth.
identifiedIntro: A purely deterministic parser would always hit a ceiling on ambiguous input, and a purely LLM-based approach would be too slow and inconsistent at volume. The answer was a hybrid: deterministic where possible, LLM-assisted where genuinely ambiguous, anchored to Eircode throughout.
builtIntro: Covison built a hybrid address intelligence pipeline that:
builtPoints: Applies deterministic parsing as the first pass
Uses controlled LLM handling for genuinely ambiguous cases
Scores confidence on every result and routes low-confidence cases to review
Anchors resolution to Eircode as the standard of truth
whyNotOffTheShelf: Standard address-validation libraries handle well-formed input but fall over on the genuinely ambiguous cases that made up most of the failure rate here. Generic LLM parsing alone would be too slow and inconsistent to run at delivery volume. The hybrid combination, with confidence scoring deciding which path a given address takes, was the part that had to be built.
productionReality: Processing about 1,000 addresses a day in production.
Confidence scoring routes uncertain cases to review instead of silently guessing.
Eircode-anchored, matching the addressing standard the business already relies on.
outcomeBullets: Accuracy improved from roughly 5 to 6 percent to over 80 percent.
Manual address correction is now the exception, not the default.
Delivery routing runs on data the operation can actually trust.
